title: Counterparty-aware economic governance
description: Everything in aegs-1, plus what a deployment paying strangers needs: a stated view of who the counterparty is and how risky this particular action looks. The difference between the two profiles is not strictness — a stricter policy belongs in a policy pack — it is how much the implementation must be able to say about the other party.

controls.note: A counterparty starts untrusted and earns standing through settled transactions. The record must distinguish a cold-start score from a measured one: an unmeasured history rendered as zero once made every advisor treat established counterparties as strangers, which is the bug the four-state rule exists to prevent.

The engine measures how risky an action inherently is; the policy decides how much of that is acceptable at a given exposure. Keeping the two apart is why a risk score is evidence rather than a verdict. Hand-weighted and never validated against outcomes — the profile requires that a score be produced and recorded, not that it be accurate.

Tightened from MUST_RECORD in aegs-1. Paying a stranger without a stated actor leaves nobody accountable for the payment. Delegation is clamped: a sub-agent may never claim more authority than its parent.

Not required even here, and the reason is worth stating plainly: sanctions screening in the reference implementation is a boolean on a vendor object — no list, no matching. A profile requiring AML would be certifying a capability nobody has. The FATF Travel Rule gap is real and named in the crosswalk: AEGS carries no originator or beneficiary data.

nonConformant: Everything that is non-conformant under aegs-1.
A decision that paid a counterparty with no trust assessment recorded.
A trust or risk score recorded as zero when it was never measured.

A sanctions bar recorded as a policy refusal. The clamp must be recorded even when a policy rule refused first — otherwise deleting the screening changes nothing observable, which is a real defect this suite has already caught once.
